note: One sentence per action of rtl_domain.hddl, with {parameter} placeholders named as the action's parameters. Hand-written for the P-series pilot (LLM_RTL_code_generation.md 8.6). The plan formats read it two ways: the NL format fills in a step's arguments, and the S2 schema fills in the parameter names, giving the action's meaning in general. No sentence contains Verilog text, with one deliberate exception: write_state_param names the idiom, a parameter and not an enum. In the pilot the executor declared states as an enum in 87% of its unplanned FSM replies and a quarter of those failed to compile, mostly from a width too small for the number of states; under a plan that said only 'a named constant', three-quarters of the replies that still used an enum failed (LLM_RTL_code_generation.md 8.6.6). The state steps give the width and each state's code, which state_encoding.py computes: left to count for itself, the executor gave ten states three bits in a quarter of its replies. The synchronous steps say outright to keep the reset out of the sensitivity list: told only that the reset is synchronous, the executor still wrote an asynchronous one in 11% of its natural-language replies and 88% of its schema ones.
legend: zero and one are the bit values 0 and 1. active_high and active_low are reset polarities. bitsN is a width of N bits. nN is the number N.

actions.analyze_choose_three_block_fsm: Build {module} as a Mealy state machine in three blocks: a clocked state register, combinational next-state logic, and combinational output logic that depends on the current state and the input.
actions.analyze_choose_moore_fsm: Build {module} as a Moore state machine: a clocked state register, combinational next-state logic, and outputs that depend only on the current state.
actions.analyze_advance: In state {state}, an input of {bit} is the next bit of the pattern, so the next state is {next_state}.
actions.analyze_stay_initial: In the initial state {state}, an input of {bit} is not the first bit of the pattern, so the machine stays in {state}.
actions.analyze_fall_back: In state {state}, an input of {bit} breaks the match. What was matched so far can still begin the pattern as far as state {fallback_state}, so {state} goes where {fallback_state} goes on {bit}: to {next_state}.
actions.analyze_match_overlapping: In state {state}, an input of {bit} completes the pattern, so the output is asserted on this transition. Matches may overlap, so {state} then goes where its fallback state {fallback_state} goes on {bit}: to {next_state}.
actions.analyze_match_from_scratch: In state {state}, an input of {bit} completes the pattern, so the output is asserted on this transition, and the machine returns to the initial state {initial_state}.
actions.analyze_restart_from_accept: Matches do not overlap, so in the accepting state {state} an input of {bit} goes where the initial state {initial_state} goes on {bit}: to {next_state}.
actions.analyze_fallback_first: State {state} has matched one bit, so its fallback state, used when the match breaks, is the initial state {initial_state}.
actions.analyze_fallback_extend: State {state} is reached from {previous_state} on {bit}. Its fallback state, used when the match breaks, is where the fallback state of {previous_state}, which is {previous_fallback}, goes on {bit}: {fallback_state}.
actions.analyze_output_in_accept_state: The output {output} is 1 exactly while the machine is in the accepting state {accept_state}, and 0 in every other state.
actions.analyze_read_transition: The specification's state table says: in state {state}, on an input of {bit}, the next state is {next_state}.
actions.analyze_extend_sequence: In state {state}, an input of {bit} is the next bit of a sequence, so the next state is {next_state}.
actions.analyze_stay_at_start: In the start state {state}, no sequence begins with {bit}, so on an input of {bit} the machine stays in {state}.
actions.analyze_keep_while: State {state} ends a sequence that goes on while {bit} keeps arriving: on an input of {bit} the machine stays in {state}.
actions.analyze_sequence_fallback_first: State {state} has matched one bit, so its fallback state, used when no sequence continues, is the start state {start_state}.
actions.analyze_sequence_fallback_extend: State {state} is reached from {previous_state} on {bit}. Its fallback state, used when no sequence continues, is where the fallback state of {previous_state}, which is {previous_fallback}, goes on {bit}: {fallback_state}.
actions.analyze_choose_counter_register: Build {module} as one clocked block that updates the count, which is held in the output register.
actions.analyze_wrap_point: When the count has reached {top}, the next count wraps around to {bottom}.
actions.analyze_choose_direction_register: Build {module} as one clocked block that steps the wave value up or down by 1, steered by a direction register.
actions.analyze_turn_point: While the direction register holds {phase}, when the wave value reaches {limit} the direction register changes to {next_phase}, and the wave value stays at {limit} for that clock cycle.
actions.write_module_header: Start the module: name it {module}, and list its ports in the order the following steps declare them.
actions.write_output_reg_decl: Declare {port} as a 1-bit output of type reg, because it is assigned inside an always block.
actions.write_output_decl: Declare {port} as a 1-bit output that a continuous assignment drives.
actions.write_output_reg_vector_decl: Declare {port} as a {width}-bit output of type reg, because it is assigned inside an always block.
actions.analyze_choose_state_encoding: Encode the states as {width}-bit binary numbers in the order they are declared, starting with {first_state} as 0.
actions.write_state_param: Declare a parameter (not an enum) for state {state}, with the {width}-bit value {code}.
actions.write_state_regs: Declare two {width}-bit registers: one for the current state and one for the next state.
actions.write_state_register_async: Write the state register: an always block triggered by the rising edge of {clock} and, asynchronously, by the {polarity} reset {reset}. While {reset} is active the current state becomes {reset_state}; otherwise it takes the next state.
actions.write_state_register_sync: Write the state register: an always block triggered only by the rising edge of {clock}. The {polarity} reset {reset} is synchronous, so do not put {reset} in the sensitivity list. If {reset} is active the current state becomes {reset_state}; otherwise it takes the next state.
actions.write_next_state_open: Begin the next-state logic: a combinational always block with a case statement on the current state.
actions.write_state_case: Add the case branch for state {state}: the next state is {next_if_0} when {input} is 0, and {next_if_1} when {input} is 1.
actions.write_next_state_default: Add the default branch: the next state is {reset_state}.
actions.write_next_state_close: End the case statement and the next-state block.
actions.write_output_open: Begin the output logic for {output}: a combinational always block.
actions.write_output_reset_clause: First, if the {polarity} reset {reset} is active, set {output} to 0.
actions.write_output_assert: Otherwise, if the current state is {state} and {input} is {bit}, set {output} to 1.
actions.write_output_default: In every other case, set {output} to 0.
actions.write_moore_output_assign: Drive {output} with a continuous assignment: it is 1 when the current state is {state}, and 0 otherwise.
actions.write_clocked_block_open_async: Begin the clocked block: an always block triggered by the rising edge of {clock} and, asynchronously, by the {polarity} reset {reset}.
actions.write_clocked_block_open_sync: Begin the clocked block: an always block triggered only by the rising edge of {clock}. The {polarity} reset {reset} is synchronous, so do not put {reset} in the sensitivity list.
actions.write_counter_reset: If the {polarity} reset {reset} is active, set {counter} to {reset_value}.
actions.write_counter_enable_open: Otherwise, if {enable} is 1, do the following.
actions.write_counter_wrap: If {counter} equals {top}, set it to {wrap_to}; otherwise add 1 to it.
actions.write_counter_enable_close: End the branch for the enable.
actions.write_generator_reset: If the {polarity} reset {reset} is active, set {direction} to {direction_value} and {wave} to {wave_value}. Otherwise do the following.
actions.write_rising_phase: Add the branch for {direction} equal to {phase}: if {wave} equals {limit}, set {direction} to {next_phase} and leave {wave} unchanged; otherwise add 1 to {wave}.
actions.write_falling_phase: Add the branch for {direction} equal to {phase}: if {wave} equals {limit}, set {direction} to {next_phase} and leave {wave} unchanged; otherwise subtract 1 from {wave}.
actions.write_direction_case_close: End the case statement, and the branch that follows the reset.
